Keep in mind the following tips are from the perspective of someone who's mostly done solo runs, but these tips should generally work for larger groups as well:

For people having trouble with getting successful runs, the number one tip I can give is to prioritize your character's attribute. Each character has a specific attribute that they scale off of for attack power, and prioritizing getting those attributes on each stage is ultimately what will make or break your runs. The attributes can be found at camps with those glowing dumbell/boot/book icons that are red/green/blue respectively. The melee character uses the red power attribute, bowman uses green attack speed attribute, and mage uses blue cooldown attribute. Stack these attributes for each character, getting at least 8-10 each stage and you should be fine throughout the run on top of getting items where you can.

As for characters, the easiest character to get a successful run on is the mage imo. He's the least dependent on items or weapons since his attribute scales his non-weapon abilities very well, and the cooldown from the blue attribute also reduces the cooldown on dodge, so he becomes the most mobile character late game because of that. He also has the best aoe damage in the game, so handling groups of mobs is much easier early game than with the other characters. The other two are also very strong but tend to be more reliant on items than the mage, and considering items are very RNG in this game whereas attributes are much less random, the mage tends to give more consistent runs overall for me. Only thing is he has the lowest health out of the characters so you may die early on in a run, but getting just a few survivability/sustain items on the first stage will go a long way. Keep your distance, get his attributes where you can, and you should have a successful run with him.

Another tip is to keep the weapon keys until the last stage since legendary weapons are what will help your damage the most for the last stage and final boss. If you stack your attributes right throughout stages 1-3 you should be fine with whatever weapon you stumble across along the way until you need legendary weapons on the last stage + final boss. Regarding weapons, another tip is to choose one or two weapons that will be your main damage weapon (be sure to choose one that corresponds for each class as well), then the rest of your weapons should specifically be chosen based on the item that's on them. If you ever see a weapon that has crit chance items or any kind of damage item on them, you should hold onto that weapon and even avoid switching it out for a legendary since you're not using that weapon for damage anyway, you're only using it for the attached item on it.

One last tip, dodging in the air is almost always better than dodging on the ground, since it adds to your current air speed and I'm pretty sure it has more invincibility frames than grounded dodge, although I could be wrong about the i-frames. You can also use it in conjunction with bounce pads to get extra speed and distance, as well as using the crossbow's right click ability to launch yourself forward if you explode it behind you while you're airborne. Dodging after the explosion will give you extra distance. Dodges will also recover cooldown while in the air, so it's possible to do multiple dodges per air time if the cooldown is low enough, you have multiple dodge charges, or if you're high enough in the air.

As for items, don't worry about them too much. You don't need to spam chests like some people are suggesting. The type of items you get is much more important than the quantity, so holding onto your gold for shops that have items you're looking for + spending them on larger chests once you have some core items you want is ideal. Core items are typically: crit chance, crit damage, attack speed, damage, resistances, lifesteal/regen/health (in no particular order, depends on what you need at the time). Most of the other items aren't necessary or are just supplementary at best. Since items are very RNG compared to attributes, it's generally smarter to prioritize attributes over items until you have enough attributes for that stage.

As for criticisms, I have a few:

Biggest issue is the difficulty, and although I'm able to go through most runs without issue once I found out what's good vs what's not so good to do, having a difficulty setting for players who aren't willing to optimize the mechanics is best. As for players who do want to optimize mechanics, adding harder difficulty settings is a good way to keep them engaged long term. Perhaps a Heat mechanic like in Hades or modifiers like in RoR2 could work. At least devs mentioned they'd add difficulty settings in a later update.

Another thing is how rare it is to find and stack crit chance in runs. It's a little odd that one of the attributes (the red power attributes) scales your crit damage, but the only way to scale crit chance is through items. Considering items are RNG in each run, it can feel very unreliable on whether or not you'll even get crit chance in a run to utilize the crit damage that one of the character's main attributes scales. There's a few items that give crit chance already, but it feels as if there's more items that give crit damage then they give crit chance, which doesn't really make sense to me. Adding a few more crit chance items would help, even if they're Epic or Legendary items. It may also help to add a conditional item that provides increased crit chance after ability use or hitting the same enemy multiple times in a row.

Only other criticism is the attribute mechanic is not explained very well in game. It's not clear how important attributes are for each character, and how each one scales off of a specific attribute. I had to uncover this information from the discord and playing the game enough even though it's a core necessity for each character's power scaling. I believe this is where a lot of people's misunderstanding of the game's difficulty spikes are coming from.

This game has a very solid base that has a lot of potential. It's mechanically engaging in a way that other roguelikes similar to it aren't. I recommend playing LORT if you're willing to sit through a few failed runs to understand how the game works and how to scale properly. Once you finally understand how to get a good run it can feel really rewarding and engaging.

It's like a t-bone steak but with no meat and no seasoning. The bones of a good game are there but the lack of substance makes it hard to play more than once after you beat the final boss for the first time. The gameplay loop is mindless due to the lack of creative ways to fine tune your build along with most items feeling like they have no real impact. Scaling is laughable unless you're playing the mage character and even then there are some late-game enemies that are incredibly annoying to deal with. I think the game could be a lot better with more time to be worked on but it's really not worth your money in the current state it's in.

The one thing the game does well over Risk of Rain 2 (its clear inspiration) is the multiplayer aspect. 8 players allowed and a pretty solid revive mechanic plus an abundance of chests means you don't really run into Risk of Rain's issue where an early death will screw you over for the rest of the run.

I struggled for the first few runs but once I watched the developers play it became easier, here's how you play the game correctly:

-Utilize speed and abilities to traverse the map as quickly as possible, use the crossbow alternate fire to rocket jump, use Astrid's dash to get yourself in the air, jump and then dodge to get more air time, bunny hop, get more jumps and dashes
-Prioritize attributes over trials/chests
-Save money for bigger chests/shops
-This one might not work with the mage, but split your attributes, Astrid with strength/agility split is better than pure strength

Overall great game with wacky humour, hopefully there will be lots of new content coming with lots of replayability, will definitely buy dlcs if you guys ever make them!

A great game once you understand the mechanics and how to proceed with the levels. This game isn't hard at all and is a fast paced roguelike game. Once you understand the characters, it will be a piece of cake. It's ONLY a piece of cake if you do well in the first level. You MUST not waste a single time doing things in the first level and have gotten enough upgrade points.

I played a lot of melee in this game and it's fun to spin2win on enemies. And I stand by that, it's just spin2win. Range does make it easier for people who can't understand the logic of how to properly dodge and move a lot. Enemies are easy to telegraph and just watch for things.

I'd say skill issue if the game is "too hard". And just play spin2win. And actually get a lot done on the first level before moving to second level, otherwise you will have a bad time.
